design: designs/2026-08-22-spine-and-lattice-program.md §5 Ring R3, incorporated by reference as the kernel workstream of designs/2026-08-22-one-trust-backward-design.md (which cites R3's ratchet machinery at its Layer-B D1(b) obligation)
rule: Every tier is derived from a COMMITTED machine-minted artifact. Authored/prose numbers never count (the house rule proven by scripts/evalir_coverage.py). Where no such artifact exists the tier is UNKNOWN with its reason and the exact command that would mint it; UNKNOWN never satisfies and never violates the ratchet. `value` is monotone UP and each `guards` entry is monotone in its stated direction; `--check` fails a regression as `regression` and any other drift as `stale`. The MINT enforces the same directions: since 2026-09-14 a bare run REFUSES to write a fallen number and names it, because `--check` compares this file against a fresh derivation and re-minting first therefore compared the file with itself. A fall lands only through `--rebase "<why>"`, which records the exact (tier, guard, direction, from, to) it forgives in `rebases` and is matched on all five, so a landed rebase can never forgive the next fall as well.
outside_the_tcb: R3 tiers are FIDELITY, not soundness. Clean's parser and elaborator sit outside the trusted computing base: everything they produce is re-checked by the kernel, so a frontend defect surfaces as a REJECTION, never as an unsound acceptance. A tier moving up means more real input gets through; it never means more is trusted.

tiers.name: everyday-language
tiers.statement: 63/63 everyday-language snippets elaborate through Clean's own frontend and are accepted by Clean's kernel.

guards.note: a snippet added to the battery that FAILS trips this even though `passed` held flat

staleness.label: STALE: measured at 410e193c1, an ANCESTOR of HEAD (4460 commits behind) — the value is true of that commit, not of HEAD

detail.comparison_basis: 38/63 snippets are byte-identical to the 2026-07-20 R100 battery (the passing set locked in commit f7f1c78bb, test_r100_everyday_lock). The 25 failing snippets were never committed — the R100 run banked them only to an ephemeral scratchpad (scratchpad/r100_battery.json), since lost — and are RECONSTRUCTED (2026-08-10) from the recorded per-snippet names and failure causes in commit f7f1c78bb's message and the R100 cluster map (24 of 25 names recorded; the unrecorded slot is unrecorded_r100_slot25, rebuilt from the missing-prelude-consts cluster description). Verdicts on the 38 locked snippets are directly comparable to 2026-07-20; verdicts on the 25 reconstructed snippets measure the same recorded failure surface but are not byte-comparable.

tiers.does_not_claim: Not soundness. The frontend is outside the TCB — every snippet's output is re-checked by the kernel, so a wrong elaboration shows up as a kernel rejection, not as an unsound acceptance. Not Mathlib: these are 63 hand-sized snippets, not library code. And only 38 of the 63 are byte-identical to the 2026-07-20 battery; the other 25 were RECONSTRUCTED from recorded names and failure causes (the original inputs were lost with an ephemeral scratchpad) and are not byte-comparable to that run.

tiers.name: universe-u2
tiers.statement: 43/54 U2 universe-level fixtures land on their pinned verdict as POSITIVE passes; the remaining 11 are MUST_FAIL fixtures pinned to refuse.

guards.note: must stay 0: every fail-pinned fixture is declared MUST_FAIL, i.e. a sound loud reject

staleness.label: STALE: measured at 1bbc6e6a8, an ANCESTOR of HEAD (3 commits behind) — the value is true of that commit, not of HEAD

detail.negative_pin_semantics: MUST_FAIL fixtures are pinned REFUSALS (rigid-refusal / ill-typed-in-Lean-too shapes). They are counted in the denominator and excluded from the numerator: a MUST_FAIL fixture that starts PASSING is a soundness event, not an improvement.

tiers.does_not_claim: Not soundness, and not universe-solver completeness. This is a 45-fixture ladder over level-inference shapes, not a corpus; passing it says those shapes elaborate and kernel-check, not that the U2 level solver is complete. The 8 fail-pinned fixtures are not counted as passes in either direction — some of them (p06, p12) are pinned to refuse FOREVER because the input is genuinely ill-typed.

detail.counting_basis_note: success_count counts --allow-sorry passes: Clean-check-report-v1 has no per-decl sorry-taint field, so sorry-tainted decls are folded into success_count and taint is only visible as the run-wide trust_summary.sorry_axioms counter recorded per file below.

tiers.does_not_claim: NOT sorry-free. counting_basis=allow_sorry_success: Clean-check-report-v1 carries no per-decl sorry-taint field, so sorry-tainted declarations are folded into the 616 and taint is visible only as the run-wide sorry_axioms counter (0). Not soundness either: 0 declarations were elaborated and then REJECTED by Clean's kernel — which is the frontend being outside the TCB working as designed, not a hole. And not Mathlib coverage: five files, chosen to span failure classes, are not the library.

staleness.label: UNKNOWN — nothing was measured, so there is nothing to be stale

tiers.reason: The milestone's counts (357/357, 1123/1123, and a 40-module / 8,908-constant cross-section) exist ONLY as prose in docs/plans/MATHLIB_KV_MILESTONE_2026-07-12.md (present in this checkout). The commands that produced them wrote their JSON to a `--out-dir` that was never committed, so no machine-minted artifact backs those numbers here. Under the house rule (scripts/evalir_coverage.py: measured rows only, authored ones never), a number typed into a plan is not a measurement, and this generator will not promote one. UNKNOWN neither satisfies nor violates the R3 ratchet.
tiers.does_not_claim: Nothing is claimed. In particular this row must NOT be read as a denial that the milestone happened — only that no committed artifact in this checkout evidences it. The neighbouring mathlib-olean-recheck-sweep-2026-07-08 row is a DIFFERENT corpus pin and is not a substitute for it.
